title: Michelin-Starred Indienne Brings Indian Fine Dining to New York's Hudson Yards
excerpt: Chef Sujan Sarkar's acclaimed Chicago restaurant opens a 34-seat New York outpost with three nine-course tasting menus, marking his return to the city where he first made his name.
body:
• Chef Sujan Sarkar has opened Indienne New York at 515 West 38th Street in Hudson Yards, offering nine-course tasting menus priced at $175 to $195 per person.
  • The Chicago original earned a Michelin star in 2023, becoming the first starred Indian restaurant in the Chicago area and one of only four in the United States.
  • Sarkar, a Kolkata native and two-time James Beard nominee, is also launching two additional concepts — cocktail bar Apas and British-Indian chophouse Elder — at the same location.
  • The opening is part of a broader push by Indian chefs to establish fine-dining Indian cuisine alongside the world's top restaurants in New York.

Chef Sujan Sarkar has returned to New York with the most ambitious project of his career. Indienne New York opened on May 28 inside Henry Hall, a luxury residential tower in Hudson Yards, bringing the Michelin-starred chef's progressive Indian tasting menu format to a 34-seat dining room at 515 West 38th Street.

The restaurant is an evolution of Sarkar's Chicago flagship, which opened in the River North neighborhood in late 2022 and earned a Michelin star within its first year — making it the first Indian restaurant in the Chicago area to receive the distinction and one of only four across the country. The Chicago location now serves 650 to 670 covers per week and has been named to "Best New Restaurant" lists by Esquire, Bon Appétit, and Robb Report. In 2026, it received the Jean Banchet Award for Restaurant of the Year.

A Tasting Menu Rooted in Two Traditions

Indienne New York offers three distinct nine-course tasting menus: non-vegetarian at $195, vegetarian at $175, and vegan at $175. A wine pairing is available for $125. Meals begin with playful, chaat-inspired courses before progressing into seasonal compositions that draw on regional Indian flavors and classical European technique.

Sarkar spent 11 years cooking in European and French kitchens before pivoting to Indian cuisine, and his food reflects that dual training. The menu balances layered spice work and varied textures with the precision and progression of a French tasting format.

"I want to be a true representation of Indian food in America, which can be on par with the top restaurants in the city and the country."

— Sujan Sarkar, Chef and Owner, Indienne

Beverage Director Chris Farrell has curated a wine program focused on small-production, terroir-driven bottles. The restaurant also offers a sustainability-focused cocktail menu that uses ingredients recycled from the kitchen, along with a customizable gin and tonic program.

A Return to New York

The Hudson Yards opening is a homecoming for Sarkar, who first established himself in New York in 2017 with Baar Baar, a modern Indian gastrobar in the East Village. That restaurant closed in August 2025, but Sarkar's national profile had grown considerably in the intervening years. He was a James Beard Award finalist for Best Chef: Great Lakes in both 2024 and 2025, and his restaurant portfolio now spans Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco, where he runs the acclaimed Tiya with his brother.

"Coming back with Indienne feels like both a homecoming and a new beginning. It means a lot to return to this city with a clearer vision of who I am and what I want to build."

— Sujan Sarkar

Indienne is the first of three concepts Sarkar plans to open at Henry Hall. Apas, a high-end cocktail bar, and Elder, a British-Indian chophouse informed by Sarkar's years working in London, are expected to follow later this summer. A fast-casual concept called Butter Chicken Social is also planned for Midtown's Shaver Hall.

Indian Fine Dining's Growing Footprint

Indienne's arrival in New York adds to a growing roster of high-profile Indian fine-dining restaurants in the city, joining Indian Accent and the forthcoming Dishoom outpost. It also reflects a broader shift in how Indian cuisine is positioned in the American restaurant landscape — moving from a category historically dominated by casual and mid-range formats into the tasting-menu tier that commands critical attention and Michelin recognition.

For Sarkar, a Kolkata native who trained across continents before building his reputation in the American Midwest, the New York opening represents both personal ambition and a larger cause: demonstrating that Indian cuisine belongs in the conversation with the world's best restaurants. The interiors, designed by MAPA Mueller, feature textured finishes, sculptural lighting, and Holi-inspired paintings by Chicago-based artist Ken Andjulis — a space calibrated to match the seriousness of the food.

Reservations are available for the 34-seat dining room. The restaurant is located on the second floor of Henry Hall at 515 West 38th Street.
